description: Procedural world from a seed (procedural-world recipe): terrain, climate, hydrology and resources after the tectonics step. Judged by the user's review; checks guard budgets and value ranges. Earth hypsometry is context for the review, not a target. Phase 4 registers one run per module that moves to the float accessors in this series; the ledger entry names the module.

review_status: Draft written by an agent on 2026-10-05 for terrain and hydrology (consolidation Phase 4, step 10). The user rewrites it; until then a verdict on it is a reading aid, not a judgement of the world.

review.question: Does the high ground of the finished world lie where the tectonic step left convergent boundaries and collision zones?
review.good: ranges and plateaus along convergent margins and sutures; plate interiors lower and smoother; the terrain passes after tectonics have not moved or erased the ranges

review.question: Do coastlines look like coasts at the scale of the grid?
review.good: irregular coasts with bays and peninsulas; no long straight edges along rows or columns, no checkerboard, no speckle of one-cell islands or one-cell seas across whole regions

review.question: Does the sea floor have shelves around the continents, deep basins and raised ridges?
review.good: a shallow shelf of varying width at the coasts, basins several kilometres deep, ridges or rises along divergent boundaries; no flat floor at one depth everywhere

review.question: Do rivers run from high ground to the sea or to a lake?
review.good: connected courses that gain flow downstream and end at a coast or a lake; no river that stops in the middle of dry land, crosses a range or runs along a row or column for a long distance

review.question: Are the large rivers where the rain is?
review.good: dense networks and the largest flows in and downstream of wet regions; deserts with few or no rivers except those fed from wet highlands

review.question: Where there are lakes, do they sit in plausible places?
review.good: lakes in basins and along rivers, with surfaces between the surrounding ground and sea level; none on slopes or summits. A world without lakes at this size is answered as unclear, not as no

review.question: Do temperature and rain respond to the terrain?
review.good: colder high ground in both seasons; wetter windward slopes and drier lee sides of the main ranges; dry belts in the subtropics and wet tropics

review.question: Is the sea surface temperature smooth and zonal where it should be, with warm tropics and cold poles in both seasons?
review.good: a broad warm band in the tropics that follows the season, gradients towards the poles, no isolated cells far from their neighbours

review.question: Is any field free of patterns that follow the grid rather than the world?
review.good: no stripes along rows or columns, no seams at the date line or the poles, no blocks at the size of a coarser solver grid, no values that jump between neighbouring cells without a cause in the terrain
